newsletter.subject: Bank of Ostravia holds at 3.75%
newsletter.text:
The Bank of Ostravia held its main interest rate at 3.75% on Thursday, as expected, after cutting it twice earlier this year.

Governor Lena Marsh said inflation had fallen to 2.9% in October, from 3.4% in June, but that wage growth of 5.1% was still too fast for the bank to cut again right away. Seven of the nine policy committee members voted to hold; two wanted a quarter-point cut.

The bank now expects the economy to grow 1.2% next year, down from its earlier forecast of 1.6%. Unemployment rose to 4.6% in October.

The next decision is on February 6.

Not financial advice.
